verdict.rationale: Galileo publishes an OpenAPI 3.1.0 spec with 202 /v2/ paths and a generated API reference with a live "Try it" runner. The SDK and official MCP server also expose core UI workflows such as datasets, experiments and prompt templates, so broad programmatic access is documented. Nothing states that the API matches the UI feature-for-feature, though, and some UI-centric features (annotation queues, alerts setup, AI Assistant) have no confirmed API equivalent. missing for 10: explicit UI/API parity statement, evidence that alerts, annotation queues and metric configuration are API-accessible, independent hands-on corroboration of parity.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: Galileo publishes a downloadable OpenAPI 3.1.0 document at its API origin (202 paths, all under /v2/)
The runner mounts client-side and executes against the production API with a real token.
With MCP, you can access Galileo's capabilities directly from your development environment, including: Creating and managing datasets, Running experiments, Setting up prompt templates
